html:
A trade unionist who led the All People's Congress, became prime minister of Sierra Leone in 1968 after a disputed election and coups, and ruled until 1985.

He made the country a republic in 1971 and a one-party state in 1978. His government ran the diamond trade through business allies, starved schools and roads, and used a party youth wing against opponents. He retired in 1985 and handed power to General Joseph Momoh. The hollowed-out state could not resist the rebels who began the civil war in 1991. See also Milton Margai and the one-party state.
